subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
intro: When a flat plane slices through a solid, the flat region where the plane cuts the solid is called a cross section. The shape of the cross section depends on the solid and on how the plane is tilted. Slicing a right rectangular prism parallel to a face gives a rectangle congruent to that face. Slicing a right rectangular pyramid parallel to its base gives a smaller rectangle similar to the base, while a vertical slice through the apex gives a triangle. The key is to picture which two-dimensional figure the plane exposes and to name it precisely using its sides and angles.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $6$ cm long, $4$ cm wide, and $3$ cm tall. A plane slices the prism parallel to its top and bottom faces. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section, and what are its dimensions?

steps: A slice parallel to a face produces a cross section congruent to that face.
The top and bottom faces are formed by the length and the width, which are $6$ cm and $4$ cm.
The height of $3$ cm runs perpendicular to this slice, so it is not part of the cross section.
The exposed figure has dimensions $6$ cm by $4$ cm. Since these are unequal, it is a rectangle, not a square.
The cross section is a $6 \text{ cm} \times 4 \text{ cm}$ rectangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $8$ in long, $5$ in wide, and $2$ in tall. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the length, slicing through the $5$ in by $2$ in face. Name the cross section and give its dimensions.

steps: A vertical cut perpendicular to the length exposes a face built from the width and the height.
The width is $5$ in and the height is $2$ in. The length of $8$ in runs perpendicular to this cut, so it is not exposed.
The four corners of the prism are right angles, so the cross section has four right angles.
The exposed figure measures $5$ in by $2$ in. Because the two dimensions are unequal, it is a rectangle, not a square.
The cross section is a $5 \text{ in} \times 2 \text{ in}$ rectangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a base $10$ ft by $6$ ft. A plane slices it parallel to the base, exactly halfway up the height. What is the shape of the cross section, and what are its dimensions?

steps: A slice parallel to the base of a pyramid produces a smaller figure similar to the base, so the cross section is a rectangle.
As you move up toward the apex, the cross section shrinks in proportion to the remaining height. At half the height the cross section is scaled by the factor $\frac{1}{2}$.
Scale each base dimension by $\frac{1}{2}$: length $10 \times \frac{1}{2} = 5$ ft and width $6 \times \frac{1}{2} = 3$ ft.
The cross section is similar to the base, not congruent to it, so its dimensions are smaller than $10$ ft by $6$ ft.
The cross section is a $5 \text{ ft} \times 3 \text{ ft}$ rectangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid is sliced by a vertical plane that passes through the apex and is parallel to a pair of base edges. What two-dimensional figure results, and why?

steps: The slicing plane passes through the apex, the single top point of the pyramid.
Because the plane also reaches down to the base, it cuts across the base in a straight segment.
The cross section therefore has one vertex at the apex and a straight base segment connecting the two points where the plane meets the bottom edges.
Three line segments enclose the region: the base segment and the two slanted sides running up to the apex.
A figure with three sides and three vertices is a triangle, so the cross section is a triangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $7$ cm by $4$ cm by $4$ cm. A plane slices it parallel to the $7$ cm by $4$ cm face. Find the area of the cross section.

steps: A slice parallel to a face produces a rectangle congruent to that face.
The slice is parallel to the $7$ cm by $4$ cm face, so the cross section is a $7 \text{ cm} \times 4 \text{ cm}$ rectangle.
The remaining $4$ cm dimension runs perpendicular to this slice and is not used in the area of the flat cross section.
Area of a rectangle is length times width: $7 \times 4 = 28$.
The area of the cross section is $28 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $9$ m long, $9$ m wide, and $2$ m tall. A plane slices the prism parallel to its top and bottom faces. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section, and what are its dimensions?
items.hint: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face. The top and bottom faces are made from the length and the width. Check whether those two dimensions are equal.

steps: A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face.
The top and bottom faces use the length and width, which are $9$ m and $9$ m. The $2$ m height is perpendicular to the slice and is not exposed.
Since both exposed dimensions equal $9$ m, the cross section is a square.
The cross section is a $9 \text{ m} \times 9 \text{ m}$ square.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $12$ in by $7$ in by $3$ in. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the $12$ in length, slicing through the $7$ in by $3$ in face. Name the cross section and find its area.
items.hint: A cut perpendicular to the length exposes a face built from the other two dimensions. Multiply those two dimensions to get the area.

steps: A cut perpendicular to the length exposes the face formed by the width and the height.
Those dimensions are $7$ in and $3$ in, so the cross section is a $7 \text{ in} \times 3 \text{ in}$ rectangle.
Area of a rectangle is length times width: $7 \times 3 = 21$.
The area of the cross section is $21 \text{ in}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a base $8$ cm by $12$ cm. A plane slices it parallel to the base, exactly halfway up the height. What is the shape of the cross section, and what are its dimensions?
items.hint: A base-parallel slice of a pyramid is similar to the base, not congruent. At half the height each base dimension is scaled by $\frac{1}{2}$.

steps: A slice parallel to the base produces a smaller rectangle similar to the base.
At half the height the cross section is scaled by the factor $\frac{1}{2}$.
Scale each base dimension: $8 \times \frac{1}{2} = 4$ cm and $12 \times \frac{1}{2} = 6$ cm.
The cross section is a $4 \text{ cm} \times 6 \text{ cm}$ rectangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid is cut by a plane that stays parallel to one pair of base edges but is tilted (not horizontal), so it is not parallel to the base and does not pass through the apex, crossing all four lateral faces. Describe the resulting cross section.
items.hint: The plane crosses all four slanted faces, so the cross section has four sides. Because the plane stays parallel to one pair of base edges, it meets the two opposite faces above those edges in parallel segments. Compare the lengths of those two segments.

steps: The plane meets all four lateral faces, so the cross section is a four-sided figure.
The plane stays parallel to one pair of base edges, so it meets the two opposite lateral faces above those edges in two parallel segments.
These two parallel segments form the top and bottom of the figure. The bottom (closer to the base) is longer than the top (closer to the apex), so they have different lengths.
The other two sides slant up toward the apex and are not parallel to each other.
A four-sided figure with exactly one pair of parallel sides of unequal length is a trapezoid, so the cross section is a trapezoid.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a base $20$ ft by $15$ ft. A plane slices it parallel to the base at $\frac{1}{5}$ of the way up from the base toward the apex. What is the shape of the cross section, and what are its dimensions?
items.hint: The scale factor equals the fraction of the remaining height up to the apex. If the cut is $\frac{1}{5}$ of the way up, then $\frac{4}{5}$ of the height remains above the base level of the cut, so the cross section is scaled by $\frac{4}{5}$.

steps: A base-parallel slice gives a rectangle similar to the base, scaled by the fraction of the height still remaining above the cut.
The cut is $\frac{1}{5}$ of the way up, so the height remaining above it is $1 - \frac{1}{5} = \frac{4}{5}$ of the total. The scale factor is $\frac{4}{5}$.
Scale each base dimension by $\frac{4}{5}$: $20 \times \frac{4}{5} = 16$ ft and $15 \times \frac{4}{5} = 12$ ft.
The cross section is a $16 \text{ ft} \times 12 \text{ ft}$ rectangle.
